locator: I capp.12–15, especially cap.15 [69988] final argument
goal: Defend or challenge the application of the no-differentiae/no-receiving-subject account of subsistent esse to the same necessary underived simple candidates. Establish whether form-multiplication by formal differences or receiving subjects is exhaustive against primitive individuation/different-essence rivals, and whether those candidates are genuinely unreceived esse rather than merely represented by equal essence/esse values. Reuse the joint two-root control and existing Q11/perfection uniqueness results; do not assume common nature or uniqueness to exclude it.
reason: The joint finite model keeps necessary actual existence, causal independence, represented simplicity/pure act, individual essence–esse and suppositum/nature identities while violating common nature and act differentiation. Compendium I12–15 supplies a substantive conditional argument, but exact applicability and individuation exhaustiveness remain independently open.
